title: Biometric Monitoring and Machine Learning to Improve Preoperative Risk Stratification in Major Non-cardiac Surgery
official: The Use of Biometric Monitoring and Machine Learning to Improve Preoperative Risk Stratification in Major Non-cardiac Surgery - Bio-Surgery Study
summary:
Many patients undergoing surgery experience complications which can lead to reduced independence and quality of life. Prior to surgery, doctors attempt to anticipate the risk of complications using information about a patient's current health, lifestyle, and medical records. The more useful health information doctors have, the more accurately they can predict whether someone is likely to develop a complication.

New technology, such as wearables (e.g., smartwatches), which are widely available and frequently used by the general public, can provide detailed health information outside of the immediate clinical environment, such as heart rate, steps taken/distance walked in a day, and sleep quality. The study is looking at whether the information from such a device could be used by doctors to more reliably predict who is likely to experience complications following surgery.

The study will consist of two phases. The first phase (piloting) will examine practical difficulties in recruiting patients and having them wear the device. In the second phase, we will assess if the information provided by the wearable is indeed able to help predict which patients are most likely to develop complications after surgery. All participants in both phases of the study will be asked to wear the device for 48 hours in the 3 months before their scheduled surgery.
